items.title: SAGE-QA: Semantic-Aware, Grounded Evaluation for Closed-Context Question Answering on SQuAD 2.0
items.summary_1line: Closed-context question answering (QA) requires a system to generate an answer strictly supported by a supplied passage, or to abstain when the passage lacks adequate evidence. SQuAD 2.0 is a widely used benchmark for...
items.editor_note: Opens the thread on evaluation: grounded, abstention-aware scoring in place of Exact Match.

items.title: JET: Just-Enough Exploration Tuning for Efficient Tool-Calling Agents in Repository-Level Question Answering
items.summary_1line: In repository-level question answering (QA), an agent explores a code repository with tools and should answer a question once enough information is gathered. Nevertheless, we find that LLM agents often continue to inv...
items.editor_note: Moves to agents: over-exploration as a cost problem in repository-level QA.

items.title: How Well Do Vision-Language Scene Graphs Serve as Memory for Embodied Question Answering?
items.summary_1line: The paper evaluates vision-language scene graphs as memory for embodied question answering, introducing an answerability metric and finding that repairs raising it from 27.2% to 37.4% do not always track gains in object F1 or QA accuracy.
items.editor_note: Shows a memory metric (answerability) can rise without matching QA accuracy gains.

items.title: Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent: Self-Structuring Learning through Question Answering
items.summary_1line: Proposes Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent, which iteratively edits a knowledge base's graph schema or linked documents using question-answer loss, and tests it on research-paper bundles, finding gains on generated questions but mixed results on human questions.
items.editor_note: Adds a self-structuring knowledge base whose gains hold on generated questions but not consistently on human ones.

editorial.tldr: This is a research-theme thread of unrelated arXiv QA papers, not a single event. It opened Nov 12 with SAGE-QA questioning Exact Match scoring on SQuAD 2.0, then JET (Nov 17) targeted tool-calling agents that keep exploring a repository after they already have enough to answer.
editorial.whats_new: Two Nov 25 papers turn to QA memory: scene-graph memory repairs lift answerability from 27.2% to 37.4% without reliably improving QA accuracy, and Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent gains on generated questions but is mixed on human ones.
editorial.why_it_matters: Across all four papers, the proxy metric (Exact Match, answerability, generated-question scores) diverges from real answer quality, so RAG and agent evals built on those proxies can misreport progress.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before trusting a QA or RAG eval gain, check it against a hand-graded sample of real user questions; treat all four papers as preprints until reproduced.

beats.headline: SAGE-QA challenges Exact Match scoring for grounded, abstention-aware QA
beats.summary: Scores whether an answer is supported by the passage or correctly abstains on SQuAD 2.0.

beats.headline: JET tunes code-repository QA agents to stop exploring once they have enough
beats.summary: Targets tool-calling agents that keep invoking tools after gathering sufficient evidence.

beats.headline: Memory structures for QA: better structure scores do not always mean better answers
beats.summary: Scene-graph memory and self-editing knowledge bases both show gains on internal metrics that do not fully carry to QA accuracy or human questions.

open_questions: How far do SQuAD 2.0 model rankings move when scored with SAGE-QA instead of Exact Match?
Is SAGE-QA's grounding check released as code that can be dropped into an existing RAG eval harness?
Does JET's early-stopping cut tool calls on repositories outside its training benchmark without lowering answer accuracy?
Does Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent improve results on human-written questions in any follow-up evaluation?
